recipes.name: Sona masoori rice idli
instructions: Wash the sona masoori rice and urad dal separately in clean water.
Soak the washed rice and urad dal in separate bowls of water for five hours.
Grind the soaked urad dal with minimal water until it forms a thick, fluffy, smooth batter.
Grind the soaked sona masoori rice separately with a little water to a slightly grainy consistency.
Combine the rice batter and dal batter thoroughly in a large deep container.
Cover the container and let the mixed batter ferment in a warm place overnight for eight to ten hours.
Gently mix the fermented batter, pour it carefully into greased idli mold cavities.
Steam the idlis in an idli steamer or cooker on medium-high heat for twelve minutes until cooked through.

recipes.name: Sona masoori rice dosa
instructions: Rinse and soak the sona masoori rice and urad dal in separate containers for five hours.
Drain the water and grind the urad dal into a perfectly fine, light, and bubbly batter.
Grind the rice into a completely smooth paste using small splashes of cold water.
Mix both prepared batters together in a large container until completely integrated.
Set the batter aside in a warm corner for eight hours to ferment and rise.
Heat a non-stick tawa over medium heat and lightly splash it with water to cool the surface.
Pour a ladle of the fermented batter in the center and spread it in a wide circular motion.
Cook until the edges lift, the underside turns golden-brown, then fold and serve hot.

recipes.name: Onion uttapam
instructions: Soak, grind, and ferment the sona masoori rice and urad dal to prepare a thick dosa batter.
Finely chop the onion, green chillies, and coriander leaves, mixing them together in a bowl.
Heat a cast-iron or non-stick griddle over medium heat.
Pour a thick ladleful of batter onto the tawa, spreading it out very slightly to keep it thick.
Immediately sprinkle a generous handful of the onion-chilli-coriander mixture evenly over the wet batter.
Gently press the toppings down with a spatula so they stick to the batter.
Flip the uttapam when the base is cooked, and cook the onion side until the onions turn golden.
Flip back to check readiness, and remove from the griddle to serve.

recipes.name: Ven pongal
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pressure cooker on low flame for three minutes until lightly fragrant.
Add the sona masoori rice to the cooker and rinse both the rice and dal together with water.
Drain the water completely, then pour four and a half cups of fresh water into the cooker.
Close the lid and pressure cook the mixture for four to five whistles until completely soft and mushy.
Once the pressure drops, open the lid and mash the rice and dal combination gently with a ladle.
In a small pan, dry-sauté the fresh curry leaves for a few seconds to release flavor.
Pour the toasted curry leaves directly into the cooked, mashed rice and dal mixture.
Stir the pongal thoroughly to distribute the flavor evenly before serving hot.

recipes.name: Rava upma
instructions: Roast the semolina in a dry pan over a medium-low flame until it becomes hot and fragrant.
Chop the onion finely and slit the green chilli lengthwise.
In another pan, dry-sauté the chopped onions and curry leaves until the onions turn translucent.
Add the slit green chilli to the pan and stir for thirty seconds.
Pour three katori of water into the pan and bring it to a boil over medium heat.
Lower the heat to low and gradually add the roasted semolina while stirring constantly with the other hand.
Cover the pan tightly and let it simmer for three minutes until all the water is completely absorbed.
Turn off the heat, mix gently to fluff the upma, and serve hot.

recipes.name: Tomato uttapam
instructions: Prepare a well-fermented thick batter using soaked sona masoori rice and urad dal.
Finely chop the tomatoes, green chilli, and fresh coriander leaves.
Combine the chopped tomato pieces, green chilli, and coriander leaves in a bowl.
Preheat a dosa tawa on a medium flame and grease it lightly.
Pour a ladle of batter onto the hot tawa without spreading it out too thin.
Spread a layer of the chopped tomato mixture evenly on top of the pancake.
Press down lightly with a spatula, flip, and cook until the tomatoes are slightly softened and caramelized.
Flip back to ensure the base is cooked completely, then lift from the pan.

recipes.name: Poha upma
instructions: Place the flattened rice in a colander, rinse it briefly under water, drain thoroughly, and keep aside to soften.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli.
In a skillet, dry-sauté the chopped onions and curry leaves on medium heat until the onions soften.
Add the chopped green chillies to the pan and sauté for another minute.
Gently fluff the damp, softened flattened rice with your fingers.
Add the flattened rice to the skillet, mixing it gently with the sautéed onions.
Cover the skillet and allow it to heat through on low flame for two to three minutes.
Remove the lid, stir gently one last time, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Vegetable uttapam
instructions: Prepare the standard idli-dosa batter using sona masoori rice and urad dal and ferment it fully.
Chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves, and grate the carrot finely.
Mix all the chopped and grated vegetables together in a bowl.
Heat a non-stick tawa over medium heat and ladle a good amount of batter to form a thick disc.
Sprinkle the vegetable mixture generously across the top surface of the pancake.
Gently press the vegetables with a flat spatula to embed them into the batter.
Flip it over when the bottom turns golden-brown and cook the vegetable side for two minutes.
Flip back to confirm it is completely cooked through, then move to a plate.

recipes.name: Millet upma
instructions: Rinse the barnyard millet thoroughly under running water and drain completely.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli.
In a saucepan, dry-sauté the chopped onions and curry leaves until they become light brown.
Add the chopped green chilli and the drained barnyard millet to the pan, stirring for a minute.
Pour two and a half cups of water into the pan and bring it to a rolling boil.
Turn the heat down to low, cover the pan with a lid, and let it cook undisturbed.
Simmer for twelve to fifteen minutes until all the water is completely absorbed and the millet is fluffy.
Remove from heat and let it sit covered for two minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Vegetable rava upma
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina until lightly toasted and fragrant, then set aside on a plate.
Chop the onion, carrot, french beans, and green chilli into small, uniform pieces.
Dry-sauté the chopped onions, carrots, and french beans in a pan along with the curry leaves.
Continue cooking the vegetables on medium flame until they become slightly tender.
Add the chopped green chilli and add three katori of water to the pan, bringing it to a boil.
Gradually pour in the roasted semolina while whisking or stirring quickly to prevent any lumps from forming.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover with a lid, and cook for three to four minutes.
Uncover, fluff the upma gently from the bottom of the pan, and serve.
